cartanDecomposition.warning: e and omega are constrained gravitational variables after symmetry breaking, not ten ordinary Yang-Mills vector bosons

infraredRequirement.masslessPole: D_GR is proportional to P^(2)/(M_Pl^2 p^2) after gauge constraints and saturation with a conserved source
infraredRequirement.fullGapConflict: replacing the graviton pole by p^2+m_g^2 changes the long-range 1/r response to exp(-m_g r)/r
infraredRequirement.lenseThirringConnection: the stationary g_0i response and its Lense-Thirring precession use the same long-range Einstein graviton sector, so a full connection gap would also Yukawa-suppress frame dragging
infraredRequirement.requiredPattern: one positive-residue massless spin-2 sector plus positive-residue positive-mass non-Einstein sectors

reducedProjectorWitness.description: an orthogonal five-dimensional mode-space proxy for the physical quadratic blocks after gauge fixing and constraint reduction
reducedProjectorWitness.interpretation: the numbers exhibit a nonempty healthy sign pattern only; a proposed action must derive its own projectors, residues and masses

stopRules.ghost: stop if any physical saturated pole has negative residue, equivalently Z_s<=0 in an already diagonal positive-norm block
stopRules.tachyon: stop if any physical pole has m_s^2<0 around the chosen vacuum
stopRules.extraMasslessMode: stop or reclassify if the zero-momentum kernel has nullity beyond the two graviton helicities without a demonstrated gauge redundancy
stopRules.higherDerivativeSpin2: stop for a local factor p^2(1+p^2/M^2) treated with ordinary Feynman poles, because its partial fractions have opposite residues
stopRules.strongCoupling: stop if a kinetic coefficient vanishes without a proven gauge symmetry and controlled nonlinear constraint algebra
stopRules.backgroundDependence: repeat the spectrum and characteristic analysis on every claimed physical background; Minkowski positivity alone is insufficient

higherDerivativeCounterexample.decision: negative-residue massive pole fails the ordinary perturbative unitarity gate

requiredDerivation: write a complete symmetry-breaking action and choose a specified vacuum
expand the coframe, Lorentz connection and selector fields to quadratic order
fix diffeomorphism and local Lorentz redundancies and solve nondynamical constraints
block-diagonalize with spin-parity projectors and saturate the propagator with allowed sources
show exactly two positive-residue massless spin-2 helicities
show every additional physical pole has positive residue and positive mass squared
recover the unsuppressed Lense-Thirring coefficient in the infrared
repeat the hyperbolicity and constraint count beyond the linearized vacuum
decision: Spin(2,3) can consistently motivate a sector-selective gap question, but the group and connection decomposition do not determine the answer; admission requires a derived massless Einstein pole and a separately positive, ghost-free, tachyon-free auxiliary spectrum
